channel.title: Make Your First Beats — by Monobox
channel.description: Drum machines and rhythm, one step at a time: how a step sequencer counts, what each drum sound does, your first beat, the classic rhythms of each genre, swing and groove, accents and dynamics, shaping the sound and turning a pattern into a whole track. Every episode ends with something to try. From Monobox, the drum machine and groovebox. Narrated with a synthetic voice.
channel.itunes:author: PDEVELOP

item.title: Shaping the sound, and from pattern to song
item.description:
Shaping the sound, and from pattern to song. Shaping the sound: Tune, length, layers and balance. From pattern to song: Variations, fills and arrangement.
Sources: - Mixed In Key, “How to arrange a Dance Music track”: https://mixedinkey.com/captain-plugins/wiki/how-to-arrange-a-dance-music-track/ - free ebook “Make Your First Beats”, chapters used in this episode
Narrated with a synthetic voice.

item.title: Swing, groove, accents and dynamics
item.description:
Swing, groove, accents and dynamics. Swing and groove: Why some beats make you move. Accents and dynamics: Loud, soft and in between.
Sources: - iZotope, “Using different tempos to make beats for different genres” (hip-hop 85–95, house 115–130, techno 120–125, dubstep 140 with a half-time feel at 70, drum and bass 174 BPM): https://www.izotope.com/en/learn/using-different-tempos-to-make-beats-for-different-genres.html - Step and beat lengths are calculated from the tempo: one beat lasts 60,000 ms divided by the BPM. - Attack Magazine, “Roger Linn On Swing, Groove & The Magic Of The MPC’s Timing” (swing on the LM-1 in 1979; 50% no swing, 66% perfect triplet swing, useful settings up to about 70%, around 54% for a light feel): https://www.attackmagazine.com/features/interview/roger-linn-swing-groove-magic-mpc-timing/ - free ebook “Make Your First Beats”, chapters used in this episode
Narrated with a synthetic voice.

item.title: How a drum machine thinks, and the kit in a box
item.description:
How a drum machine thinks, and the kit in a box. How a drum machine thinks: Steps, patterns and tempo. The kit in a box: What each sound does.
Sources: - Roland, “TR-808” (introduced in 1980, analog synthesis instead of samples, about 12,000 units made, discontinued in 1983): https://www.roland.com/us/products/rc_tr-808/ - Wikipedia, “Roland TR-808” (step sequencer; influence on hip-hop and electronic dance music): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roland_TR-808 - iZotope, “Using different tempos to make beats for different genres” (hip-hop 85–95, house 115–130, techno 120–125, dubstep 140 with a half-time feel at 70, drum and bass 174 BPM): https://www.izotope.com/en/learn/using-different-tempos-to-make-beats-for-different-genres.html - Step and beat lengths are calculated from the tempo: one beat lasts 60,000 ms divided by the BPM. - free ebook “Make Your First Beats”, chapters used in this episode
